title: Easter Sunday: The Resurrection of the Lord
gospelText: On the first day of the week, Mary of Magdala came to the tomb early in the morning, while it was still dark, and saw the stone removed from the tomb...
reflection: The empty tomb is the starting point of our faith. We are invited to see and believe that love has conquered death.
prayerText: Risen Jesus, deepen my faith in Your Resurrection.
prayerResponse: Help me to live as a child of the light. Amen.

title: Second Sunday of Easter (Divine Mercy Sunday)
gospelText: Jesus came and stood in their midst and said to them, 'Peace be with you.'
reflection: Even in our doubt and fear, Jesus enters our locked rooms to bring us His peace and mercy.
prayerText: Merciful Jesus, I trust in You.
prayerResponse: Grant me Your peace that passes all understanding. Amen.

title: 11th Sunday in Ordinary Time
gospelText: This is how it is with the kingdom of God; it is as if a man were to scatter seed on the land...
reflection: Like a tiny mustard seed, God's kingdom grows quietly and invisibly in our hearts and in the world.
prayerText: Lord, sow Your Word in my heart and make it fruitful.
prayerResponse: May Your kingdom come in my words and actions today. Amen.

title: 12th Sunday in Ordinary Time
gospelText: On that day, as evening drew on, Jesus said to his disciples, 'Let us cross to the other side.' A violent squall came up and waves were breaking over the boat... Jesus woke up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, 'Quiet! Be still!' The wind ceased and there was great calm.
reflection: In the midst of life's sudden storms, we may feel overwhelmed and ask, 'Lord, do You not care?' But Jesus is in the boat with us, inviting us to move from fear to profound trust in His presence.
prayerText: Jesus, speak Your peace to the storms in my heart and quiet my anxieties.
prayerResponse: Quiet my fears, Lord, and anchor my trust in You. Amen.

title: 13th Sunday in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jairus, a synagogue official, fell at Jesus' feet and pleaded, 'My daughter is at the point of death. Come lay Your hands on her that she may live.' On the way, a woman touched His cloak and was healed of her hemorrhage. Jesus told Jairus: 'Do not be afraid; just have faith.'
reflection: Both the suffering woman and the grieving father show us the power of reaching out to Jesus in active faith. He is the Lord of healing and life, telling us to not let fear consume us.
prayerText: Lord Jesus, bring Your healing touch to my wounds and give me the grace to trust Your timing.
prayerResponse: I believe, Lord; strengthen my faith and heal my heart. Amen.

title: Monday of the 11th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said to his disciples: 'You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth. But I say to you, offer no resistance to one who is evil. When someone strikes you on your right cheek, turn the other one to him as well.'
reflection: Jesus calls us to break the cycle of retaliation and meet hostility with unexpected generosity and love.
prayerText: Lord, give me a heart that forgives readily and loves unconditionally.
prayerResponse: Grant me the grace to overcome evil with good. Amen.

title: Tuesday of the 11th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said to his disciples: 'Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be children of your heavenly Father...'
reflection: God's love is universal, shining on both the good and the bad. We are invited to reflect this perfect, unconditional love.
prayerText: Father, help me pray for those who make my life difficult and love them with Your heart.
prayerResponse: May Your perfect love transform my heart today. Amen.

title: Wednesday of the 11th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said: 'Take care not to perform righteous deeds in order that people may see them... but when you pray, go to your inner room, close the door, and pray to your Father in secret.'
reflection: True righteousness is a matter of the heart, seen by God alone. Seek His approval rather than human praise.
prayerText: Lord, purify my intentions. Let my prayers and good deeds be done solely for Your glory.
prayerResponse: Father, who sees in secret, draw my heart close to Yours. Amen.

title: Thursday of the 11th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said to his disciples: 'In praying, do not babble like the pagans... This is how you are to pray: Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name...'
reflection: The Our Father is the perfect blueprint of prayer, focusing first on God's glory and then on our daily trust in His provision and forgiveness.
prayerText: Father, teach me to pray with deep trust, resting in Your fatherly care.
prayerResponse: For Yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.

title: Friday of the 11th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said: 'Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and decay destroy... But store up treasures in heaven... For where your treasure is, there also will your heart be.'
reflection: Our hearts naturally follow what we value most. Let us invest our time and energy in eternal things like love, mercy, and faith.
prayerText: Lord Jesus, help me detach from worldly possessions and seek the true riches of Your kingdom.
prayerResponse: Be my only treasure, Lord, now and forever. Amen.

title: Saturday of the 11th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said: 'No one can serve two masters... Do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink... Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given you besides.'
reflection: Anxiety stems from wanting to control the future. Jesus invites us to trust that our heavenly Father knows our needs and will sustain us day by day.
prayerText: Holy Spirit, grant me the peace of children who trust completely in their Father's love.
prayerResponse: I seek Your kingdom first, Lord; take care of all the rest. Amen.

title: Monday of the 12th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said to his disciples: 'Stop judging, that you may not be judged. For as you judge, so will you be judged... Why do you notice the splinter in your brother's eye, but do not perceive the wooden beam in your own?'
reflection: Before we rush to criticize others, we must look honestly at our own faults and approach others with humility and compassion.
prayerText: Lord, remove the wooden beam of pride from my eyes so I can see others with Your mercy.
prayerResponse: Help me to judge myself with honesty and others with charity. Amen.

title: Tuesday of the 12th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said: 'Do to others whatever you would have them do to you. This is the law and the prophets... Enter through the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the road broad that leads to destruction...'
reflection: The Golden Rule is a simple but radical way of living. The path of true discipleship is narrow and requires conscious choices to walk in love daily.
prayerText: Jesus, guide my steps today through the narrow gate of humility and service.
prayerResponse: Lead me, Lord, on the path that leads to life. Amen.

title: Solemnity of the Nativity of St. John the Baptist
gospelText: When the time arrived for Elizabeth to have her child she gave birth to a son... They were going to call him Zechariah after his father, but his mother said, 'No, he will be called John.'
reflection: John the Baptist was sent to prepare the way for Jesus. His life reminds us of our own call to point others to Christ and decrease so He may increase.
prayerText: St. John the Baptist, pray for us that we may prepare the way of the Lord in our homes and hearts.
prayerResponse: Lord, make me a witness of Your saving light. Amen.

title: Thursday of the 12th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: Jesus said: 'Everyone who listens to these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock. The rain fell, the floods came... but it did not collapse; it had been set solidly on rock.'
reflection: Hearing the Gospel is not enough; we must put it into practice. Acting on Christ's teachings builds a spiritual foundation that no storm can shake.
prayerText: Lord Jesus, establish my life on the solid foundation of Your words and Your love.
prayerResponse: You are my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer. Amen.

title: Friday of the 12th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: A leper came, did him homage, and said, 'Lord, if you wish, you can make me clean.' Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, 'I will do it. Be made clean.'
reflection: Jesus is not afraid of our uncleanness, brokenness, or sin. When we approach Him with simple faith, He reaches out to heal and restore us.
prayerText: Lord Jesus, I come to You just as I am. If You wish, You can make me clean.
prayerResponse: Reach out Your hand and heal my soul, O Lord. Amen.

title: Saturday of the 12th Week in Ordinary Time
gospelText: When Jesus entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him and said, 'Lord, my servant is lying at home paralyzed... I am not worthy to have you enter under my roof; only say the word and my servant will be healed.'
reflection: The centurion's faith is so profound that we repeat his words at every Mass. We trust in the power of Jesus' word to heal even across distance.
prayerText: Lord, I am not worthy to receive You, but only say the word and my soul shall be healed.
prayerResponse: Jesus, I trust in the power of Your healing word. Amen.

title: First Sunday of Advent
gospelText: Stand erect and raise your heads because your redemption is at hand.
reflection: Advent is a time of waiting and vigilance. We prepare our hearts to welcome Christ both at Christmas and in His glory.
prayerText: Come, Lord Jesus, prepare my heart.
prayerResponse: Help me to stay awake and prayerful. Amen.
